summary: Punch tells a joke about a witness whose slang the judge cannot understand; the photographer is arranging the session.

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you, we was on a job one time, and so one of the boys went out for the end of the morning going to work. And while he's on his way to work, he met two ladies, and the two ladies was fighting, one big, stark lady and a little small lady. Well, by that time, the little lady gets loose from the big lady, and she runs out and gets her brick, as they call it, and hit the big lady in the head and cut her head and started to bleed. By that time, the policeman come by. And so the only man that could pick up was this guy on the street going to work, 4 in the morning. Well, so he cast him down, and the judge said, well, I got you for a witness. Now, tell me just what happened. Well, he got to talk, this gay talk to the judge, you see. So he told the judge, he said, listen, judge, he said, I was puffing down this broad with this first brightness, and I hadn't run up on those two broads. They were scrambling right briefly, little stuff stuff And the judge said, how did you say that again? He said, I was puffing down this bird on this face brightness. And I happened to run up on those two torts. Those two torts were scrambling right briefly. The little torts scooped down, get a ground apple, and the big torts in the keg, starts the top not leaking. So the judge said, well, I want them to lock you up just about until time so you can talk American and I can understand what you're saying. And then, he said, that's the minute, judge. I'm trying to tell you. I was walking down the street going to wake. This morning, early, and running up on these two weapons. And they was fighting. The little woman got stuck the big woman in the head and starts her head to bleed. That's all I know, judge. He said, oh, I thought you'd come straight after a while.
Oh, that's great. That's funny. You want to wash your hands, sir? Want your hat? Should we get his hat on, Wilson? I don't want to have.
